tagline: Up the Rogue with the mail, down the Coquille.
intro: From Gold Beach the byway goes up the Wild and Scenic Rogue to Agness, where the Illinois comes in, then turns north through the Siskiyou National Forest. The forest boundary ends just short of Powers, and from there the road follows the South Fork Coquille down past Myrtle Point, where the forks of the river come together, to the town of Coquille, some 82 miles in all.
Thirty winding and sometimes dangerous miles between Gold Beach and Agness were reason enough for the district to keep a one-room school open at the far end. It had two rooms.

moments.title: Agness
moments.text: Named for the first postmaster's daughter Agnes and misspelled ever since, Agness is served by one of the last two rural mail boat routes in the country, up the Rogue from Gold Beach.

moments.title: Illahe
moments.text: After years of asking, Elijah Price got a trial mail boat in 1895 for perhaps eleven families and no towns, and named his log-cabin post office for the Chinook Jargon word for land.

moments.title: Powers
moments.text: Named in 1914 for Albert H. Powers of the Smith-Powers Logging Company, the town keeps what is thought to be the region's oldest pioneer dwelling beside a railroad museum.
